title: BANG, PARCHE and TINOSA against two convoys
eyebrow: Luzon Strait · Coordinated attack group, Capt. G. E. Peterson
lede: Every mark is a position or attack typed into the boats' war patrol reports, beside the Japanese record of the same minutes. Times are converted to GMT so the three boats, who kept different clocks, share one timeline.

notes.head: Reading the map.
notes.text: Positions are the boats' own dead reckoning and star sights, and three navigators never quite agree, so the same convoy appears in slightly different places in each report. Lines between positions are straight; where a boat actually went in between is not recorded. Dashed outlines mark entries the report itself contradicts, kept with the reason.

notes.head: Clocks.
notes.text: BANG kept zone K (−10) and PARCHE zone I (−9); TINOSA kept zone H (−8) on station. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9). On 29–30 April the target ship's own log and BANG's attack sheets agree to within one to seven minutes once both are in GMT.

notes.head: Sources.
notes.text: War patrol reports, NARA microfilm M1752 (BANG 74802746, PARCHE 74828582, TINOSA 74856363). Nittatsu Maru's movement log and the 1st Surface Escort Division war diary via JACAR (National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy lists and the 3–4 May sinking times from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

boats.name: PARCHE
boats.co: LCdr L. P. Ramage; pack commander Capt. G. E. Peterson aboard

actions.label: 29–30 April 1944
actions.route: Takao → Manila. Departed Takao 1300 on 28 April.
actions.ships_note: Merchant ships as listed by combinedfleet.com; other lists add Yashima and Hakka Maru.
actions.outcome: Japanese loss list: Takegawa Maru (1,930 GRT) and Nittatsu Maru (2,859 GRT), both to BANG. No loss matches PARCHE's or TINOSA's attacks next morning; the rest reached Manila on 2 May.
actions.sil_note: Silhouettes show the kind of ship (fleet submarine, destroyer, escort, auxiliary gunboat, merchant ship, tanker, fighter aircraft), not each one's own outline, and are not to scale.

events.title: Log
events.text: Received contact report from BANG; increased speed to 17 knots on course 180°T.

events.outcome: Takegawa Maru (1,930 GRT), TAMA-17; sank 2240 I (J04). BANG was then depth-charged by Harukaze.

events.title: Depth charges
events.text: heard series of depth charges - searched around again and found a fleet type destroyer ... range 1500 yards.

events.title: Takegawa Maru
events.text: At 2201 on the 29th, at N 19°20′ E 118°50′, No. 10 ship Takegawa Maru was torpedoed by an enemy submarine
events.original: 二九日二二時〇一分北緯一九度二〇分東経一一八度五〇分ニ於テ第十番船竹川丸敵潜水艦ノ魚雷攻撃ヲ受ケ

events.title: Ordered 400 ft
events.text: she swung hard toward me ... range 1200 yards I had to give up and ordered 400 ft.

events.title: Passing 300 ft (2)
events.text: Two depth charges set shallow exploded directly over head as we passed 300 ft.

events.title: Depth charges (20)
events.text: About 20 more depth charges within the next 45 minutes. None very close.

events.title: Takegawa Maru
events.text: At 2240 she finally sank
events.original: 仝二二時四〇分遂ニ沈没セリ

events.title: Ordered 450 ft
events.text: Having heard nothing for 30 minutes carefully reloaded three (3) torpedoes at 450 ft. then planed up to periscope depth.

events.title: Nittatsu Maru
events.text: By 2350 rescued 56 of Takegawa Maru's crew and passengers
events.original: 仝二三時五〇分竹川丸乗組員及便乗者中五六名ヲ救助セリ

events.title: 30th Air Base
events.text: Heavy rain in the morning prevented convoy air cover; weather at sea to the south cleared from about 1500; anti-submarine patrols of sectors 5, 6 and 7 saw nothing

events.text: Radar interference, so assumed it to be PARCHE or BANG. Kept at a safe range. We should have IFF on SJ Radar for use with coordinated attacks.

events.title: Log

events.title: Attack 2 (narrative)
events.text: Fired 3 at tanker (hits 23-10-23), 3 at AK astern; tanker sank; position is where the tanker sank
events.outcome: TINOSA saw her first target, a tanker, hit under the bridge and the bow and sink. Toyohi Maru was an ore carrier; the secondary source's 0008 I is one minute before TINOSA's first hits.
events.doubt: position of the target, not TINOSA

events.title: Log
events.text: Observed first hit in Tanker under her bridge … One hit heard but did not see it, as was watching Tanker go down. Sank: Lat. 20-51N Long. 118-02E.

events.title: Attack 5
events.text: Torpedo attack No. 5
events.outcome: JANAC credits BANG with Kinrei Maru, but the secondary source's 0106 I for her sinking is the minute PARCHE fired her Attack 2. BANG fired at 0232 I, after PARCHE and TINOSA had scattered the convoy (her own words); the losses timed about 0300 (J15) are the nearer match. BANG's Attack 5 (0232 I) is 28 minutes before the secondary source's "about 0300" for Shoryu and Daiyoku Marus, which it credits to PARCHE.
